expect: Explain the command and supported scopes without acquiring source or spawning specialists.
Do not require a review target as a condition for answering help.
Proceed with source identity, complete preliminary declaration reading and the eight-base-question plan.
Select contextual aspects from source; do not treat a small fixture as reason to omit base coverage.
Do not require a PR URL or an extra approval to begin the requested review.
Apply applicable defaults and record confirmed no team policy.
Do not ask the user to create a policy file or look for a substitute instruction filename.
Distinguish inaccessible policy from confirmed absence; report the policy gap.
Do not silently apply defaults or a working-tree/proposed policy; defer dependent advice while retaining independently supported progress.
Deliver a complete report with no accepted recommendations without another discovery pass.
Retain identity, actual coverage, scope limits and no-candidate outcome; empty file-map and implementation-order tables are unnecessary.
Do not claim perfection or independent bug/test/security validation.
Deliver or accurately explain a partial review with unfinished independent coverage and the concrete capability/result gap.
Do not convert absence into a completed no-candidate result, simulate a specialist, or wait for a known impossible result.
Continue the planned collection without introducing a mandatory handoff/recovery phase.
Do not create a recovery file in the reviewed tree or treat continuation guidance as required startup reading.
Treat the summary as an index, not sufficient evidence for acceptance or completion.
Expose lost snapshot/results as gaps, do not silently retarget or reconstruct nonexistent recommendations from counts.
Do not promise unsupported persistence or write recovery files into reviewed source.
Reuse the target and scope already supplied; no repeated PR/target question or confirmation.
Proceed read-only with the selected naming scope rather than the full default lens set.
Ask specifically for the missing review target.
Do not invent a repository, start broad searching, or load the full review catalog before the target is known.
Apply the named Go refinement in its scope and deliver it to the naming specialist.
Do not infer disables or unrelated conventions, and do not let the illustration replace the actual rule.
Keep the selected pinned refinement; disclose the proposed disable only as a policy change.
Do not let proposed-source policy disable the review of itself or silently substitute it for the selected policy.
